correctness.rationale: The identity (x^-1+1+x)^3=(x^-3+1+x^3)+3h(x) with h=x^-2+2x^-1+2+2x+x^2 is exact. Raising to successive ternary powers modulo nine yields a first-order correction in adjacent digits. Support bounds below 3^(i+1) separate the two-digit local block; the six exact constant terms J_{a,b} form [[2,2],[6,8],[16,24]]. The only surviving corrections with one digit two are at that digit and its immediate higher neighbor; with at least two digits two they vanish modulo nine. Exhaustive ternary-word counting then yields the two formulas for all L>=2. The packaged verifier independently checks the identity, local constants and 19,683 coefficients up to 3^9 against exact recurrence; those finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new conclusion is an explicit if-and-only-if ternary-neighbor classification of valuation one for ordinary central trinomial coefficients, with closed counts for every ternary length. Primary sources establish only the no-digit-two criterion modulo three (Deutsch–Sagan and Noe), while algorithms that can compute prime-power congruences (Rowland–Zeilberger) do not state or simplify to the exact claimed classification in inspected text. Direct central trinomial treatment by Rampersad–Shallit addresses moduli three and five; Mikić 2023 excludes the ordinary coefficient in its valuation theorem. No published-finding corpus match or OEIS exact-table coverage was found after actual stated queries, but priority cannot be certified from searches.
residual_risks: Rowland–Zeilberger and related general automata may yield the classification after an unrecorded specialization; priority is not established by failure of keyword search.
Further papers on residues of the ordinary central trinomial sequence modulo nine or stronger digit-carry classification might be unindexed or inaccessible.
The same-model proof and computational checks are not independent mathematical auditing.

value.rationale: The classical trinomial modulo-three zero set has an exact Cantor-digit description; its first higher-prime-power layer is a motivated, genuinely distinct divisibility invariant. The theorem classifies exactly the valuation-one indices for every nonnegative n, identifies a previously non-obvious immediate-neighbor restriction, and gives closed census formulas for every 3^L, including their L times 2^L growth. This is a complete natural classification, not a small numerical improvement or arbitrary slice; higher valuations deliberately remain open.
